threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused at bus stops, checking your phone for the TfL app like it’s your lifeline. Locals just know when to hop on.
Last night on the 196, a bloke serenaded the whole bus with a bagpipe. Half the passengers were bemused, the other half filmed it. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I walked past the kiez and saw a group of kids setting up a makeshift outdoor cinema in the park, complete with blankets and popcorn.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can grab a currywurst from a street stand while checking out art galleries. It's like street food meets culture, all in one block.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local if they can spot the BART delays before they hit the news—every Friday, the same train jam in the Tube.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy calmly juggling on the bus while a toddler tried to eat his shoelaces. Classic Muni chaos, but somehow everyone was just rolling with it.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí and tapas, but it's the local bakeries on Carrer de Joan Blanques that serve the best morning croissants.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they hesitate at pedestrian crossings, waiting for non-existent traffic lights.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus will take you to where you need to go on time, bless your heart. It's all about the overland or a good pair of shoes here.
Caught a glimpse of a guy in a duck costume dancing with a street performer at Brixton bus stop last weekend. Only in South London, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a spontaneous Blockade in the street for a rave, locals bringing out potties and a grill, and everyone just vibing like it's a normal Saturday.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it’s common to see people sipping coffee at the corner while discussing last night’s underground film screening — a vibe unlike anywhere else.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows to avoid the BART during rush hour, especially after a loud bang or smoke at Civic Center. They know it’s not just transit; it’s survival.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a lady singing opera on the 31 while a guy next to her tried to sell his mixtape. Just another Tuesday in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists assume all the trendy bars in Gràcia are overpriced. But there are hidden gems where you can still grab a caña for under 2 euros if you know where to look.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewilderment at the lack of a timetable at the bus stops. The locals just know when to show up.
